items.label: H2
items.content: Getting Started - Step One

items.label: T3
items.content: cancel

items.label: T4
items.content: The following steps should give you a feel for how you go about building your Constituent Database and your Supporter Database.

items.label: T5
items.content:
Acquire and prepare your voter data.  Unless you have run for office before, you may not have a Constituent Database.   In that case, you may purchase voting records from the County Registrar of Voters.  Most are available in electronic form for a very reasonable price (often under $100 for a CD with full county information).  
Voting records may come in many different formats - Tawala can import two different formats: Excel and CSV (Comma Separated Values).  If your records are in a different format, they are many different services and tools available on the Internet for converting your data into one of these. 
Once you have your data ready, press Submit.

items.label: H3
items.content: Getting Started - Step Two

items.label: T6
items.content: cancel

items.label: T7
items.content:
Import your data into the temporary Import File. Because importing can be hazardous, it is the only step that cannot be taken from within this application. You will need to go to your CampaignDashboards Project Details page. Here is link to take you there: new-window

It will open in a separate window so it's OK to click on it - you will still be able to refer to these directions.

Your Project Details Page should look a bit like this: (If you were not already logged into CampaignDashboards.com, you are first taken to the LogIn page and asked to enter your user name and password - your should have gotten those when Customer Service helped you set this application up.)

The top Form is entitled ImportFile. If the number under the Responses heading is not zero, it means that the file already has some contents in it. It is generally a good idea to save those contents before taking the next steps unless you know that they are no longer of any value. That's what the third Actions icon on the right side of the page does, the sheet of paper with a green right arrow on it - it saves or exports all the records in the ImportFile form. (If you hover over an icon, an explanation of what it does should appear.) Click on the Export icon and follow the simple imstructions that appear to save a copy of the file data on your own computer.

items.label: T8
items.content: You may wonder what the Export button under the Project Actions Header does and why you aren't using that.  Well, CampaignDashboards contains dozens of Forms, and that buttons saves all of them at one time.  That's saving a good deal more information than you need to at the moment.

items.label: T9
items.content:
Once you have saved any data in ImportFileI, it is OK to purge or delete that data from the form.  That's what the fifth icon in the row is for (a little garbage can).  Click on that, and the number under responses should change to zero.
Now you are ready to Import your data.  The fourth icon from the left (a square with a blue bar at the top and a small upward green arrow below) is the Import button.  Click on that and follow the directions, assigning each field of data that you wish to import to a different column in ImportFile.  Keep track of what you put in each column.  Some contents (like Home Phone versus Office Phone) are easy to confuse.
Once you are done, you should receive a message telling you how many records were imported.  That number should match the number under the Responses tab in the picture above.  And you can look at a sample of the data by clicking on the first icon, the magnifying glass.
At this point you have completed your voter data import.  Press Submit to continue.

There are DataBase records in the database of which DataBase still need to be indexed.

Indexing is the process of determining all of the unique values in every fields o make it easier to search and sort records. For example, an index of city names will only have a single instances of "Los Angeles" in its records, not one for each vote who lives in LA, as is the case in the main constituent database.
